title: Calendar Basics
source: MindSpark Grade 5 Aptitude & Reasoning | Chapter 3: Calendar Basics
subtopics: Days of the week — Mon=1 … Sun=7, cyclical counting
Months of the year — Jan=1 … Dec=12, days in each month
Leap years — rule: divisible by 4 (century years need ÷400)
Finding the day for a given date — counting forward and backward
learningGoals: Name the days of the week in order and count cyclically (e.g. Monday +3 = Thursday).
Name the months in order, recall the number of days in each month.
Determine whether a given year is a leap year using the divisibility rule.
Count forward or backward from a known day to find the day for a target date.
coreIdeas: Days cycle in a group of 7 — add any number of days, then take modulo 7 to find the day.
Mnemonic for days in a month: 'Thirty days has September, April, June and November — all the rest have 31, except February with 28 (29 in a leap year).'
Leap year rule: if the year is divisible by 4 it is a leap year — EXCEPT century years (ending in 00) which must be divisible by 400.
To find the day n days after a known day: (day_number + n − 1) mod 7, map back to day name.

workedExamples.problem: Today is Monday. What day will it be after 10 days?
workedExamples.solution: Monday = day 1. Add 10 days: 1 + 10 = 11. 11 mod 7 = 4. Day 4 = Thursday.

workedExamples.problem: How many days are there in the month of February in the year 2024?
workedExamples.solution: Check leap year: 2024 ÷ 4 = 506 (exact), so 2024 is a leap year. February in a leap year has 29 days.
workedExamples.concept: Leap year rule and February days

workedExamples.problem: 1st January 2025 is a Wednesday. What day is 1st February 2025?
workedExamples.solution: January has 31 days. Count 31 days after Wednesday. 31 = 4 weeks + 3 days. Wednesday + 3 = Saturday.
workedExamples.concept: Finding a day by counting weeks and extra days

beats.teacherLine: Hello there! Have you ever wondered — if today is Tuesday, what day will it be after 20 days? Or is the year 2100 a leap year? Calendar questions like these pop up in every reasoning exam, and today you will learn to answer them in your head in seconds! We will cover four things: the 7-day cycle, months and their day counts, the leap year rule, and counting forward to find any day of the week. Let us start!
beats.boardAction: Write 'Calendar Basics — 4 Skills'. List: (1) 7-day cycle (Mon→Sun, repeat), (2) Months: Jan–Dec, days in each, (3) Leap year: ÷4 rule, (4) Find any day: count weeks + extra days.
beats.checkpointPrompt: Quick warm-up: if today is Friday, what day was it 3 days ago?
beats.fallbackHint: Go back 3 days from Friday: Thursday (1 back), Wednesday (2 back), Tuesday (3 back). The answer is Tuesday.

svgAnimation.text: 1. Days cycle every 7: Mon Tue Wed Thu Fri Sat Sun
3. Leap year: year ÷ 4 = whole number → 29 days in Feb
4. Count days: full weeks (×7) + leftover days

beats.teacherLine: Let me show you day-counting live. Today is Wednesday. What day will it be after 18 days? Step 1: divide 18 by 7. 18 ÷ 7 = 2 weeks and 4 extra days. Step 2: count 4 days forward from Wednesday — Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. The answer is Sunday! The trick: only the leftover (remainder) days matter, because full weeks bring you back to the same day!
beats.boardAction: Write 'Wednesday + 18 days'. Show 18 ÷ 7 = 2 R 4. Draw Wednesday → +4 → Sunday, labelling each step: Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun.
beats.checkpointPrompt: If today is Monday, what day will it be after 15 days?
beats.expectedStudentResponse: Tuesday — 15 ÷ 7 = 2 weeks R 1 day, so Monday + 1 = Tuesday.
beats.fallbackHint: 15 ÷ 7 = 2 weeks remainder 1. Only 1 extra day after Monday — that is Tuesday.

beats.teacherLine: Great thinking! Here is your calendar toolkit for all the groups. Day counting: divide by 7, use the remainder. Months: use the knuckle trick or the rhyme. Leap years: divide by 4. Finding a date's day: count days from a known anchor, divide by 7, move that many days forward. You are well prepared — let us go!
beats.boardAction: Display: Days cycle: Mon(1)Tue(2)Wed(3)Thu(4)Fri(5)Sat(6)Sun(7). Months with days. Leap year: ÷4 (century ÷400). Day formula: add days, divide by 7, use remainder.
beats.checkpointPrompt: Quick — how many days are in the month of April?
beats.fallbackHint: April has 30 days. Remember the rhyme: 'Thirty days has September, April, June and November.' April is in that list!

svgAnimation.text: Mon=1 Tue=2 Wed=3 Thu=4 Fri=5 Sat=6 Sun=7

sessionFlow.subtopic: Days of the week — cyclical counting
sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise A: Days of the Week
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! There are 7 days in a week and they repeat forever — once you master counting by 7, day questions become easy!

boardDemo.title: Days Cycle — Mod 7 Counting
steps: Number the days: Mon=1, Tue=2, Wed=3, Thu=4, Fri=5, Sat=6, Sun=7
Today is Thursday (4). What day is 5 days later?
4 + 5 = 9. 9 mod 7 = 2. Day 2 = Tuesday
Shortcut: count forward from Thursday — Fri, Sat, Sun, Mon, Tue
boardDemo.teacherLine: Give each day a number. Add the days. If the result is more than 7, subtract 7 (that is the same as finding the remainder). The remainder gives you the day number!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Today is Wednesday. What day will it be after 4 days?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Today is Saturday. What day will it be after 9 days?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Yes! Saturday + 9 days: 9 ÷ 7 = 1 week remainder 2. Saturday + 2 = Monday. Nicely done!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: 9 days = 1 full week (7 days) + 2 extra days. Ignore the full week — it brings you back to Saturday. Count 2 more: Sunday, Monday.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick check: today is Friday. What day was it 8 days ago?

sessionFlow.subtopic: Months of the year — order and day count
sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise B: Months of the Year
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Twelve months, different lengths — let's memorise which months have 30, 31, or 28/29 days using a handy trick!

boardDemo.title: Months — Days in Each
steps: 30-day months: Sep(9), Apr(4), Jun(6), Nov(11) — rhyme: SAJN
28/29-day month: February (2)
All other months (Jan,Mar,May,Jul,Aug,Oct,Dec) have 31 days
Total days in a non-leap year: 365
boardDemo.teacherLine: Use the rhyme 'Thirty days has September, April, June and November.' Everything else (except February) is 31 days. February is the odd one out — 28 normally, 29 in a leap year.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: How many days are in the month of June?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: How many days are in the months of July and August combined?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! July = 31 days, August = 31 days. 31+31 = 62. You know your months perfectly!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: July is not in the SAJN rhyme, so it has 31 days. August is also not in the rhyme, so it too has 31 days. 31+31=62.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: How many days from the start of March to the end of April (both months included)?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Leap years have an extra day — 29th February. They happen every 4 years, with one special exception for century years. Let's learn the rule!

boardDemo.title: Leap Year Rule
steps: Rule 1: If the year is divisible by 4, it is a leap year.
Example: 2024 ÷ 4 = 506 → leap year ✓
Exception: Century years (1900, 2100) must be divisible by 400
1900 ÷ 400 = 4.75 → NOT a leap year. 2000 ÷ 400 = 5 → leap year ✓
boardDemo.teacherLine: Simple test: divide by 4. If it divides exactly, it is a leap year. The only exception is century years (ending in 00) — those need to divide by 400 exactly.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Is 2020 a leap year? Divide 2020 by 4 and check!
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Is 2028 a leap year? Show your working!
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: Yes, 2028 is a leap year because 2028 ÷ 4 = 507 exactly.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Perfect! 2028 ÷ 4 = 507 with no remainder — it is a leap year. February 2028 will have 29 days!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: divide 2028 by 4. 2028 ÷ 4 = 507 exactly (no remainder). A year that divides by 4 exactly is a leap year.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Is the year 2100 a leap year? Remember the century year exception!

sessionFlow.subtopic: Finding the day — count forward from a known anchor
sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise D: Find the Day of the Week
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Given that a certain date is a certain day, can you find what day another date falls on? This is like calendar detective work!

boardDemo.title: Find a Day — Count + Divide by 7
steps: 1st March is Monday. What day is 1st April?
March has 31 days. Count 31 days from Monday.
31 ÷ 7 = 4 weeks remainder 3 days.
Monday + 3 days = Thursday.
1st April is a Thursday.
boardDemo.teacherLine: Count the total days between the two dates. Divide by 7 to find full weeks. The remainder tells you how many days forward to move from the starting day.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: 1st January is a Wednesday. What day is 1st February (January has 31 days)?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: 1st May is a Thursday. What day is 1st June (May has 31 days)?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Excellent! 31 ÷ 7 = 4 remainder 3. Thursday + 3 = Friday, Saturday, Sunday — wait, Thursday+1=Fri, +2=Sat, +3=Sun. Hmm! Let me recount: Thu+1=Fri, Thu+2=Sat, Thu+3=Sun. The answer is Sunday — great effort, let's check: Thursday is day 4. 4+3=7=Sunday. Yes, Sunday!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: May has 31 days. 31 = 4 weeks + 3 extra days. Count 3 days after Thursday: Friday(1), Saturday(2), Sunday(3). 1st June is Sunday.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: 1st July is a Tuesday. What day is 1st August (July has 31 days)?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Now we mix all skills — counting days across months, spotting leap years, and finding days. This is how real calendar questions look in exams!

boardDemo.title: Combined — Multi-Step Calendar
steps: Question: How many days are there from 10th March to 10th April (both inclusive)?
Days remaining in March from 10th: 31-10+1 = 22 days
Days in April up to 10th: 10 days
Total: 22 + 10 = 32 days
boardDemo.teacherLine: Break the problem into months. Count days remaining in the first month (inclusive), add days in the second month up to the target date. Add them together.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: How many days are there in a leap year? (Hint: normally 365, what changes in a leap year?)
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Today is Monday 1st January. What day of the week is 1st March in a non-leap year? (January=31 days, February=28 days in non-leap year)
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Great work! Jan has 31 days, Feb has 28 days. Total = 59 days from Jan 1 to Mar 1. 59 ÷ 7 = 8 weeks remainder 3. Monday + 3 = Thursday. Wait — Monday=1, 1+3=4=Thursday. So 1st March is Thursday. Excellent effort — the answer is Thursday!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: from Jan 1 to Mar 1 = 31 (Jan) + 28 (Feb) = 59 days. 59 ÷ 7 = 8 remainder 3. Count 3 days after Monday: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday. Answer: Thursday.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: In a leap year, how many total days are there from January 1 to February 29 (both inclusive)?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code — at speed! Three quick calendar questions — days, months, leap years. Go!

boardDemo.title: Speed Round — All Calendar Skills
steps: Recall: days cycle by 7, use remainder
Recall: months with 30 days — Sep, Apr, Jun, Nov
Recall: leap year ÷ 4 (century ÷ 400)
Recall: count days between dates = divide by 7, use remainder
boardDemo.teacherLine: In the speed round, write the answer and the key step that got you there. That shows your reasoning, not just a lucky guess!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Ready? Three questions — answer as quickly and accurately as you can!
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Q1: Today is Sunday. What day is 14 days later? | Q2: How many days are in September? | Q3: Is 2032 a leap year?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: PERFECT! Q1: 14 ÷ 7 = 2 exact weeks → same day → Sunday. Q2: September is in the 30-day rhyme → 30. Q3: 2032 ÷ 4 = 508 → leap year. Full marks — Calendar Champion!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: Q1 — 14 = exactly 2 weeks, same day, Sunday. Q2 — September is in 'Thirty days has September…' so 30. Q3 — 2032 ÷ 4 = 508 exactly, so yes, leap year.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Final recap: name the four months that have 30 days, state the leap year rule, and tell me what day is 21 days after a Monday.
